correctness.rationale: For N=3M the Fourier eigenvalue and quadratic-form coordinate change are exact. Eisenstein prime splitting proves the unrestricted norm divisor formula; completing the square shows any forbidden integer triple has Q at least ceil(3(M+1)^2/4), with an explicit forbidden triple at equality. The uniform limiting CDF follows from exact circular-cap geometry of a regular simplex and an absolute O(N^-1) discrepancy bound for convex bounded-perimeter lattice sections. The cusp constant 6 sqrt(2) follows from the arccos endpoint expansion. The packaged standalone checker passes 12252 supplementary assertions; it is not used as proof for infinitely many N or m.

originality.rationale: The classical Eisenstein divisor formula is explicitly treated as prior knowledge. The assessed new statement combines the sharp first failure of unrestricted representations on nonnegative homogeneous three-torus shells, the uniform-rate global eigenvalue distribution and the cusp at the limiting sharp cutoff. Full texts of the 2023 triangular Fourier series paper and the 2022 Robin triangle manuscript concern Dirichlet/Robin eigenfunction series on a physical triangle, not the graded torus shell; Pinsky (1980) is known to cover Eisenstein quadratic eigenvalues for a planar triangle but its full text remains unavailable. Targeted mathematical-literature comparisons did not yield an equivalent or stronger torus-shell result. Undiscovered general lattice-simplex formulas remain possible.

A general lattice-simplex restriction formula could imply the sharp clipping theorem without using this terminology.

value.rationale: This is an exact spectral classification of a natural Fourier grading: fixed homogeneous degree on the three-torus is a canonical analytic frequency shell. A sharp integer cutoff identifies when the unrestricted Eisenstein number-theoretic degeneracies cease to be valid; independently the all-degree spectral measure has an explicit square-root singularity at the corresponding normalized boundary. The joint integer and continuum transition is structurally motivated and not merely a small numerical table, a known divisor count or a renamed value.
